summary: Bernhard Karlgren worked in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915) and later held posts at Uppsala University (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (1974–1993), and Leipzig University (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Brooklyn Polytechnic, NYU, UCLA, and under Zen teachers Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk, and held posts at Heidelberg University and Leiden University.

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and others. He held academic posts at Halle and served as professor at Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady, and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum.

Bettina Bäumer is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, Munich, and under Swami Lakshman Joo, and held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Vienna, and other institutions.

Bettine Birge is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studied under Wm. Theodore de Bary and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle. She held posts at Halle, Hamburg, the University of London, Oxford, and the University of Colombo.
Betty Jean Shefts was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Ngawang Nyima.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad.

Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University and founded Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith, serving as its headmaster from ~1921 to 1926.
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested as head of the Research Department in 1989.

Bhagwan Dash was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, and worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University (~1884). He held posts as a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (1882) and member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Bhajagovinda Ghosh was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and on the editorial board of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and held posts at the Central Institute of Hindi and Kendriya Hindi Shikshan Mandal.
Bhau Daji was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who completed his studies at Elphinstone College (~1840–1843) and Grant Medical College (~1845–1850).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peradeniya and Marburg. He has held positions at Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.
